premises.text: Government policy is still created and communicated as unstructured text, so the public barely engages despite large personal income impacts
premises.evidence_span: we've been creating and communicating government policies through unstructured text documents

premises.text: A microsimulation of the US economy from tax returns and census data lets people configure policies and see projected impacts on real people and maps
premises.evidence_span: merging millions of tax returns and census records to create a model of the US economy

premises.text: Citizens can endorse preferred outcomes so governments see analytics that shape policy (aided representation)
premises.evidence_span: this response gets recorded on the government's analytics, helping them shape policies around what people want

premises.text: Users can simulate alternative tax rates and budget line items in real time against large populations
premises.evidence_span: it'll calculate this new rate against the spending patterns of over 6 million people

premises.text: Outline is a turnkey government solution cheaper than bloated SAP/Accenture-style consulting tools that the public cannot access
premises.evidence_span: Outline, though, is a turnkey solution that not only saves governments money, but produces better governing

value.text: Participation in government becomes direct, intelligent, and easy as part of daily internet use
value.evidence_span: making participation in government direct, intelligent, and easy

secondary_value.text: Better, cheaper governing for states and cities
secondary_value.evidence_span: saves governments money, but produces better governing

notes: Text-document inertia and public non-engagement folded as one problem (§4.1.6).
